records.title: Lawrence JH, Hamilton JG. Aviation Medicine and High Altitude Physiology. Monthly Progress Report No. 24. OSRD. 1 October 1945.
records.locator: Progress Report No. 24, pp. 1–2, items 1, 4–5 (NLM images 893–894)
records.note: The investigator report counts 398 man-flights across seated arm-exercise conditions at varying effort and strain. It gives changes in symptoms and incapacitation without arm denominators or exact outcome counts. Page 2 lists Henry's article as submitted for consideration.

records.title: Cook SF. Role of exercise, temperature, drugs and water balance in decompression sickness. In Fulton JF, ed. Decompression Sickness. Saunders. 1951.
records.locator: Printed p. 232 (PDF p. 257), exercises I–VI and reference 145
records.note: Cook explicitly attributes the exercise table to Henry. Approximately seventy men completed repeated exposures at 38,000 ft. The Number of Subjects column totals 390 across six exercises. The relationship to the 398 man-flights in the progress report and the exact denominator for each reported percentage are unresolved. No case counts were reconstructed.
records.extraction_method: manual verification against the original table image

records.title: Fulton JF. Report to Dr. Lewis H. Weed concerning the trip of the Subcommittee on Decompression Sickness to California, 24 June – 3 July 1944. Yale Aeromedical Research Unit Report 37. 8 July 1944.
records.locator: Printed and PDF p. 9, San Diego flight account
records.note: The July 1944 visit report describes classified subjects flown at 35,000 ft in San Diego and pilot bends despite one hour of preoxygenation. It provides no case count, exact denominator or complete observation window. This account belongs to the existing San Diego aircraft research program. The complete PDF was checked against the page image after Firecrawl recovered the first eight pages.
